dimensions.boundary: When you profiled feature extraction on the XNCC device, where did latency actually concentrate — and what did you change in the pipeline specifically because of what you saw in that profile?

dimensions.label: INT8 Quantization and Pruning for 4x Compression
dimensions.resume_anchor: 4× model compression via INT8 quantization and pruning for scalable, low-power, low latency AI application
dimensions.surface: You achieved 4× compression through INT8 quantization and pruning — what was the uncompressed model size before those two techniques were applied?
dimensions.mechanism: INT8 quantization and pruning interact differently on accuracy — on your AudioSet and UrbanSound8K targets, which technique degraded accuracy more, and what did you do to recover it while keeping the footprint under 200 KB?
dimensions.boundary: When you calibrated INT8 quantization for the XNCC NPU specifically, what data did you use for the calibration set and what accuracy drop did you observe versus the float32 baseline before you accepted the quantized model?

dimensions.label: Proprietary XNCC Environment Deployment and Latency Validation
dimensions.resume_anchor: custom classifier for a 700 MHz DSP + 16 MB NPU in the proprietary XNCC development environment, accomplishing <10 ms latency
dimensions.surface: The XNCC environment is proprietary — how did you move a TensorFlow Lite-Micro model into it, and what format did the XNCC toolchain actually consume?
dimensions.mechanism: Edge Impulse targets standard embedded SDKs, but XNCC is proprietary — where specifically did that mismatch create integration work, and how did you resolve it?
dimensions.boundary: Your <10 ms latency claim is on a 700 MHz DSP — how did you measure that number on the XNCC device, and what was the variance across inference calls under different audio input conditions?

dimensions.label: 95%+ Classification Accuracy Claim on AudioSet and UrbanSound8K
dimensions.resume_anchor: achieving top notch-industry standards of 95%+ classification accuracy on AudioSet, UrbanSound8K
dimensions.surface: Your 95%+ accuracy figure spans two datasets — were you evaluating on the full AudioSet eval set or a subset, and what class count did your classifier target?
dimensions.mechanism: AudioSet is heavily class-imbalanced — what metric did you actually optimize during training, and does your 95%+ figure reflect per-class accuracy, top-1 accuracy, or something else?
dimensions.boundary: After INT8 quantization and pruning, how much did accuracy drop from your float32 baseline on UrbanSound8K specifically, and what was the threshold below which you would have rejected the compressed model?

recovery.short_answer: Let's ground this in the XNCC device specifically — name one number from your latency profiling: what was the slowest single inference call you measured on the 700 MHz DSP?
recovery.honest_gap: Fair — which part of this pipeline do you have the clearest hands-on ownership of: feature extraction, the quantization step, or the XNCC deployment itself?
recovery.claim_conflict: Your resume says <10 ms latency and 200 KB footprint on a 700 MHz DSP, but what you just described would require significantly more compute or memory — walk me through where those numbers actually came from.
recovery.metric_risk: You cited 95%+ classification accuracy — what was the exact test split, how many samples, and was that number measured on the quantized model running on the XNCC device or on the float32 model in a desktop environment?
recovery.overclaim_risk: You mentioned low-power AI application — what was the actual power budget in milliwatts you were targeting on the XNCC device, and how did you measure or estimate power draw during inference?
recovery.bridge: That covers the edge deployment work at Optek well — let's shift to your research work on Multimodal Bird-Sql Benchmark Construction And Schema Design, where you were designing SQL schemas and evaluation protocols for vision-language models.

candidate_q4_options: The 16 MB NPU on the XNCC device — how much of that 16 MB did your model and runtime actually consume, and what determined the ceiling?
You used Edge Impulse for SDK deployment targeting a proprietary XNCC environment — what did Edge Impulse give you that you could not get from the TFLite-Micro toolchain directly?
Your pipeline targets real-time inference — what audio window size and hop length did you use for feature extraction, and how did those choices interact with your <10 ms latency constraint?
You cite 4× compression from both quantization and pruning together — if you had to attribute the compression ratio, roughly what fraction came from pruning versus INT8 quantization alone?

focus_areas.label: Multimodal Bird-Sql Benchmark Construction And Schema Design
focus_areas.anchor_context: Reconstructed BIRD-SQL benchmark (12,751+ question-SQL pairs, 95+ databases) with vision+NLP annotation, schema-aware prompting, and OCR validation.
sub_focuses: relational schema design and complex hybrid SQL query authoring
schema-aware prompt engineering and OCR validation for multimodal annotation
resume_snippets: pioneered BIRD-SQL dataset (12,751+ question-SQL pairs, 95+ large databases) by integrating vision + NLP annotation
Designed relational DB schemas, and created complex hybrid SQL queries to introduce reasoning challenges for vision-language models
focus_areas.why_priority: Different domain (text-to-SQL + multimodal benchmarking) with specific dataset scale claims and schema design decisions
focus_areas.opener: In the BIRD Vision benchmark work, you integrated vision and NLP annotation across 12,751+ question-SQL pairs — walk me through the specific annotation decision that was hardest to get right.

dimensions.label: Schema Design and Complex Hybrid SQL
dimensions.resume_anchor: Designed relational DB schemas, and created complex hybrid SQL queries to introduce reasoning challenges for vision-language models
dimensions.surface: You designed schemas specifically to introduce reasoning challenges for VLMs — what structural property in a schema makes it harder for a vision-language model to traverse than a flat table?
dimensions.mechanism: A hybrid SQL query targeting a VLM reasoning challenge has to stress something the model can't shortcut. In the BIRD-SQL schemas you designed, which join pattern or subquery structure consistently exposed model failures, and why does that structure create ambiguity the model can't resolve from surface tokens alone?
dimensions.boundary: Across 95+ databases in BIRD-SQL, schema heterogeneity must have forced tradeoffs in how you defined foreign-key relationships for annotation consistency. Name a specific schema decision you made that constrained the SQL query space in a way you didn't anticipate.

dimensions.label: VLM Failure-Point Evaluation Protocols
dimensions.resume_anchor: designing evaluation protocols to identify model failure points
dimensions.surface: The evaluation protocols you designed were meant to identify model failure points — what distinguishes a question-SQL pair that reliably triggers a failure from one that just happens to get a wrong answer?
dimensions.mechanism: When you categorized failure points across the 12,751+ pairs, what signal told you a model was failing on visual grounding specifically versus failing on SQL structure — and how did your protocol separate those two causes when the model output was just an incorrect SQL string?
dimensions.boundary: Evaluation protocols can reward models that pattern-match to schema names rather than reason over content. In the BIRD-SQL benchmark construction, how did you verify your protocol wasn't measuring schema-string recall instead of the multimodal reasoning it was designed to test?

dimensions.label: Schema-Aware Prompt Engineering
dimensions.resume_anchor: using schema-aware prompt engineering, OCR validation, annotating complex multimodal inputs
dimensions.surface: You used schema-aware prompt engineering during annotation — what information from the schema was the prompt carrying that a generic NLP prompt would have left out?
dimensions.mechanism: Schema-aware prompting for a benchmark with 95+ databases means the prompt had to generalize across heterogeneous table structures. What specific schema element, when included in the prompt, most improved annotation consistency across databases — and what was the tradeoff of including it?
dimensions.boundary: Schema-aware prompts can introduce annotation bias if the model over-indexes on column names surfaced in the prompt. In your BIRD-SQL annotation work, how did you detect and handle cases where the prompt itself was leaking the answer structure to the annotator model?

dimensions.label: OCR Validation for Multimodal Annotation
dimensions.resume_anchor: integrating vision + NLP annotation for advance database queries and OCR validation
dimensions.surface: OCR validation was part of your annotation pipeline — at what stage of annotation did OCR output feed into the question-SQL pair construction?
dimensions.mechanism: OCR output for database-related visual inputs like table screenshots or chart images introduces noise that propagates into SQL references. In the BIRD-SQL annotation work, how did your validation step prevent an OCR transcription error from corrupting the ground-truth SQL a question was paired with?
dimensions.boundary: OCR confidence scores vary significantly across image types. In your annotation pipeline, how did you set the threshold at which an OCR result was flagged for human review versus accepted automatically — and what evidence did you use to calibrate that threshold?

recovery.short_answer: Take the BIRD-SQL schema design specifically — pick one table you designed and tell me what made the foreign-key structure in that table harder for a model to reason over than a simple join would have been.
recovery.honest_gap: That's a fair place to draw the line — given what you did own in this project, which part of the schema design or evaluation protocol do you feel you understood most deeply and could defend technically?
recovery.claim_conflict: Your resume says you designed relational DB schemas to introduce reasoning challenges, but your answer describes following an existing schema structure — which parts of the schema were you actually authoring versus inheriting from the BIRD-SQL source dataset?
recovery.metric_risk: The 12,751+ pairs is the scale claim — how was a question-SQL pair counted as valid, what was the rejection rate during annotation, and what denominator produced the final benchmark number?
recovery.overclaim_risk: You used the phrase schema-aware prompt engineering — in your specific implementation, what schema fields were injected into the prompt, in what format, and how did that change the model output compared to a prompt without them?
recovery.bridge: That gives me a solid read on the benchmark construction work. Let's move to a system you built rather than evaluated — on the AIGC Video Generation And Editing Pipeline On Google ADK at Wondershare Filmora, I want to dig into how the seed-based generation workflow held up under real editing constraints.

candidate_q4_options: In the BIRD-SQL benchmark, you had 95+ large databases — how did you ensure a question-SQL pair written against one database schema couldn't be answered by a model that had only seen a structurally similar schema elsewhere in the dataset?

The benchmark reconstruction produced 12,751+ pairs — what was your quality control mechanism for catching annotation errors that were internally consistent but semantically wrong relative to the visual input?

OCR validation across visual database inputs would frequently produce a false positive where extracted text looks correct but references the wrong table cell. Walk me through a specific case like that from the BIRD-SQL work and how your pipeline handled it.

strengths: Dimension boundary probes are genuinely ownership-gated: the XNCC memory-profiling question, the seed-vs-prompt-steering tension, and the OCR false-positive probe all require hands-on work to answer rather than documentation reading.

issues: All three openers are 'walk me through' variants — they invite narrative rather than force an immediate analytical or causal position, costing roughly 1.5 points on opener quality and preventing an above-8.5 overall score.

repair_instructions: Replace all three openers with hypothesis or causal-challenge framing. Example for Area 1: 'You claim seed diffusion preserved character identity across edits while prompt steering changed scene content — those two goals are in direct tension in a latent diffusion model. What specifically in your implementation resolved that tension?' This forces an immediate analytical position without inviting a tour of the system.

Fix Area 3 opener attribution: replace 'At BIRD-SQL' with 'On the HKU-Columbia-Alibaba-CUHKSZ project' or 'In the BIRD Vision benchmark work' to correctly anchor to the research context listed on the resume.

Replace Area 2 recovery overclaim_risk probe: remove the 'video manifold' reference entirely and substitute a probe grounded in the Optek work, e.g., 'You used the phrase low-power AI application — what power budget in milliwatts were you actually targeting on the XNCC device, and how did you measure power draw?'

Elevate the Area 1 opener by anchoring to the 35% cost figure as a causal challenge rather than a system tour: 'Your resume attributes ~35% cost reduction to seed-based regeneration versus full Veo-3 resampling — what specific architectural decision drove most of that saving, and what would it cost to undo just that one decision?' This satisfies the causal_validity first-dimension requirement and is answerable only by the engineer who built the cost model.

candidate_state.implementation_anchor: I created a seed regeneration technology that generates seed values to preserve character consistency in video generation systems.

coverage_map.application_question: Imagine your PM comes to you tomorrow and says: 'The seed regeneration system you built for single character consistency works great in our internal demos — but we're launching a social storytelling feature where users upload videos with multiple characters, and every character needs to stay consistent independently across scenes, even when they appear together in the same frame. We need this live in 6 weeks.' How would you extend your existing seed-based consistency pipeline to handle this multi-character scenario?
coverage_map.implementation_anchor: I created a seed regeneration technology that generates seed values to preserve character consistency in video generation systems.

dimensions.label: Per-Character Seed Isolation
dimensions.description: Tests whether the candidate understands that a single global seed can no longer serve multiple characters — each character needs its own seed identity that travels with it across scenes without polluting other characters' conditioning signals
expected_approaches: Maintain a seed registry mapping character ID to its dedicated seed value, updated per scene
Use separate conditioning channels or prompt tokens per character to prevent seed interference
Assign character-specific LoRA or embedding anchors tied to each seed identity
dimensions.surfacing_question: If two characters share the same frame, what stops one character's seed from drifting or bleeding into the other character's appearance?

dimensions.label: Character Detection & ID Assignment
dimensions.description: Tests whether the candidate thinks about the upstream problem — before you can track seeds per character, you need to reliably detect and re-identify each character across scenes, especially when they appear and disappear
expected_approaches: Run a face/person detection model per scene to assign stable character IDs before seed lookup
Use visual embedding similarity (e.g., CLIP or ArcFace) to re-identify characters across scene cuts
Allow users to manually tag characters in the first frame as a fallback identity anchor
dimensions.surfacing_question: If a character disappears for three scenes and then comes back, how does your system know it's the same character and should use the same seed?

dimensions.label: Seed Conflict in Shared Scenes
dimensions.description: Tests awareness that co-occurring characters in the same generation frame create a tension — the model receives multiple seed conditioning signals simultaneously and the candidate should reason about how to prevent degradation
expected_approaches: Decompose generation into character-masked passes and composite in latent space
Use weighted prompt steering that allocates conditioning budget proportionally per character region
Generate characters separately and blend at the pixel/latent level using segmentation masks
dimensions.surfacing_question: When two characters are in the exact same frame and you're feeding both of their seeds into the generation step, what could go wrong with the output?

dimensions.label: Non-Technical User Accessibility
dimensions.description: Tests whether the candidate connects backend seed complexity to the UI layer they already built — multi-character seed management must stay invisible to non-technical users while still being controllable
expected_approaches: Auto-detect characters and show a simple character card UI where users can name or approve detected identities
Provide a 'lock character' toggle that freezes that character's seed across the whole project
Visualize seed consistency confidence per character with a simple indicator so users know when drift is happening
dimensions.surfacing_question: A non-technical user uploads a video with three characters — how does your interface let them manage character consistency without exposing any of the seed mechanics underneath?

dimensions.label: Graceful Degradation on Edge Cases
dimensions.description: Tests junior-level awareness of what happens when the system is uncertain — crowd scenes, partial occlusions, or new characters mid-video — and whether the candidate thinks about safe fallback behavior
expected_approaches: Fall back to global seed consistency when character count exceeds a threshold (e.g., crowd scenes)
Flag low-confidence character re-identifications for user review rather than silently assigning a wrong seed
Allow users to manually split or merge character identity tracks when auto-detection fails
dimensions.surfacing_question: What should your system do when it genuinely cannot tell if a character in a new scene is one of the existing characters or someone brand new?
